text:
nina: ACME onboarding hit a burst of 429s during embedding load test. They reported TLS handshake errors from their edge before the 429s. Need quick triage.

sam: Got it. Are they using our SDK or calling the API directly? sample payload?

nina: Node SDK v1.8.2 behind custom proxy. Batch size 100, concurrency 12. Pasted minimal repro.

```js
client.embeddings.create({ model: 'open-embed-v2', input: [...], batchSize: 100 });
```

devon: Two likely causes: proxy opening new TLS sessions per request (handshake churn) and very high concurrency causing service backpressure -> 429.

sam: Ask them to run a single curl test to isolate gateway vs upstream:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":["test"]}'
```

nina: They ran curl — it succeeded. SDK through gateway fails with `tls: handshake failure` then 429.

devon: Confirms gateway. Recommend: enable keepalives and TLS session resumption on gateway, reduce SDK concurrency to 4 and batch_size to 32, enable jittered backoff.

onboard-bot: Created ticket RW-5510: "ACME gateway handshake churn -> 429s" and cc'd infra.

sam: Ops approved a 24h onboarding bump while they patch gateway. I'll add a short runbook for edge gateway customers.

nina: Thanks — ACME will test keepalives and report back."
